## How to use this doc

Same convention as `docs/build/v1.6.2.md`: each item is self-contained. Per CLAUDE.md, state model/effort + rationale before editing, keep the build green, add tier-1 tests alongside sync/money logic, one green commit per item, **no commit/push without explicit permission**. Update each item's **Status** line as work progresses, and add the commit hash when done.

**Status legend:** `NEEDS DECISION` · `NEEDS INVESTIGATION` · `TODO` · `IN PROGRESS` · `FIXED (uncommitted)` · `DONE <hash>`

**Build order (post-grilling):** **8 → 9** (badge fixes together) **→ 7** (settlement label) **→ 1** (Notes pin: the schema/migration slice) **→ 2** (rollover reset) **→ 10** (currency doc/screen sync — trivial, independent). Bugs **4, 5, 6** run as a **parallel repro-only pass** (no code) — Item 4 first given its severity (blocks clean sign-out). Item 3 is deferred to the Post-V1 Horizon (#14) — not built in this batch.

## Item 1 — Pin functionality in Notes

- **Status:** DONE `70835c9` — see **ADR-0040**. On-device verified by Alvin.
- **Raw feedback:** "no pin 👎👎 the message is has virus" (beta tester, garbled) — flagged against version `0.1.0-staging`.
- **Dev comment:** Pin functionality in Notes.

**Decision:** a synced **`is_pinned` boolean** column on the `notes` row. **Multiple** pins; pinned notes hoist into a "Pinned" section on top; ordering otherwise unchanged (`ORDER BY isPinned DESC, updatedAt DESC, createdAt DESC`). Pin/unpin reuses the existing `UpsertNote` write path (LWW sync, no new sync logic). Consequences accepted: you can only pin notes **you own** (partner notes are read-only replicas, ADR-0005), and pinning a **shared** note propagates the pin to the partner's copy. Rejected local-only per-user pin (fights `applyPullBatch`'s REPLACE, needs a separate store, buys only private-pinning-of-partner-notes). Full rationale + build shape in **ADR-0040**.

## Item 2 — Reset rollover should apply to the primary month target

- **Status:** DONE `29cc402` — see **ADR-0041** (amends ADR-0036 follow-up).
- **Dev comment:** Reset rollover should happen to the primary month target, not before or after.

**Root cause (confirmed in code):** `BudgetsViewModel.resetRollover(row)` passes the displayed month **M**, but `ResetBudgetRolloverUseCase` clears `rolloverEnabled` on **M+1** (creating that row if absent). So the user resets while looking at M, but M still shows its wrong accumulated carry — only M+1 changed. **Decision:** clear `rolloverEnabled` on **M itself** (upsert M), delete the next-month create branch, keep the `require(budget.rolloverEnabled)` guard. Accepted consequence: M's rollover toggle now reads OFF after reset (honest: "this month no longer carries anything in"). Rejected the persisted "carry = 0" marker variant (ADR-0036 deliberately avoided a marker). Full rationale + test deltas in **ADR-0041**.

## Item 3 — Currencies other than PH Peso

- **Status:** DEFERRED — moved to **Post-V1 Horizon #14**. Not a V1.6.3 build item.
- **Dev comment:** Different currencies other than PH Peso.

**Decision (scope, deferred):** true multi-currency (per-account currency, FX conversion) is **out** — it collides with the PHP-only V1 convention and is a quarter of work (currency field on every money row, FX, and deciding what the *combined couple view* even sums). What ships eventually is **display-symbol-only**: a single cosmetic setting that swaps the `₱` glyph for another symbol, **no conversion**, all amounts still one currency underneath. **Chosen at onboarding.** In the combined view it's the **viewer's** symbol (personal display pref, like theme) — explicitly cosmetic, **not** reconciled across the couple, so a partner picking a different symbol just sees their own label; we accept the "it's a symbol, not a conversion" imprecision rather than build couple-level reconciliation for a Horizon cosmetic. Captured as Horizon #14.

## Item 4 — "Paid for partner" not syncing

- **Status:** DONE `dfc2929` — migration applied to staging, columns verified live via PostgREST probe: `partner_debts.source_transaction_id`, `partner_debt_payments.is_netting`, `partner_debt_payments.counter_debt_id` all present. No Kotlin change. Highest severity in this batch (blocked clean sign-out; data-integrity).
- **Dev comment:** Paid for partner doesn't seem to be syncing, every time i have to sign out with paid for partner entry, it says something isn't synced up, no matter how long i wait.

The sign-out guard (ADR-0021) warns when `pending_sync` rows remain. A "paid for partner" action (`PaidOnBehalfUseCase`) creates the user's EXPENSE transaction **and** a couple-owned `partner_debt` row (plus possibly a netting payment). **Top hypothesis:** the couple-owned `partner_debt`/payment row stays `pending_sync=1` and never pushes — a **silent push failure**, most likely an **RLS/FK rejection on staging** (schema/policy mismatch) or the couple-owned row being **omitted from the dirty-rows push selection**. Possibly an ADR-0009 ordering edge (debt pushed before its couple/FK dependency) or an ADR-0005 redaction edge.
**Repro:** on-device — record a paid-for-partner entry → trigger sync → watch Logcat around the push cycle → inspect the local DB for which table still has `pending_sync=1` after sync. Then check that table's syncer + the server RLS policy.

**Findings (repro):** No emulator was attached, so instead of Logcat this was confirmed **directly against staging PostgREST** using the app's staging anon key and the app's exact push payload shapes — which reproduces the precise HTTP error `SupabasePartnerDebtRemoteSource.push` receives (stronger than a Logcat line, since it's the wire response itself).

- **Root cause = staging schema drift.** Staging's debt tables are missing three columns that `supabase/schema.sql` defines but **no file in `supabase/migrations/` ever adds** (grep confirms: `source_transaction_id` and the netting columns exist only in `schema.sql`, added way back in the V1.3 debt-netting commit `b153e01`, and were never migrated onto the live staging DB). Column probes via PostgREST `select=`:
  - `partner_debts` → **missing `source_transaction_id`** (all other 10 columns present).
  - `partner_debt_payments` → **missing `is_netting` and `counter_debt_id`** (the ADR-0019 #9 netting columns). Notably the ADR-0019 #14 settlement columns `payor_account_id` / `payor_txn_id` / `receiver_txn_id` **are** present — so a later settlement migration reached staging but the netting + paid-for-partner columns never did.
- **The failing write.** A paid-for-partner debt (`PaidOnBehalfUseCase`) always sets `sourceTransactionId = transaction.id` (non-null). `PartnerDebtDto` serializes that as `source_transaction_id`, and `client.from("partner_debts").upsert(rows)` gets rejected by PostgREST with **HTTP 400 `PGRST204` — "Could not find the 'source_transaction_id' column of 'partner_debts' in the schema cache."** Reproduced live; the column check fires at schema-cache/parse time, *before* RLS. (Control probe: the identical payload with `source_transaction_id` omitted gets past the column check and only trips RLS `42501` — i.e. a real couple member's write with that column absent would succeed.)
- **Why it wedges forever (matches "no matter how long I wait").** `BaseTableSyncer.push()` calls `remotePush(dirty)`; on the thrown `PGRST204` it never reaches `clearPending(acked)`, so the debt row keeps `pending_sync=1`. `SyncEngine.pushAllIsolated()` catches it as the first `pushError`, finishes the other tables, pulls, then rethrows → `SyncState.Error`. The user's EXPENSE transaction pushes fine (that table is unaffected); only the couple-owned `partner_debts` row is stuck. Because the column will never appear on its own, every retry re-throws the same `PGRST204` — the row is permanently dirty, and the ADR-0021 sign-out guard keeps reporting "something isn't synced." This is the reported symptom exactly. (Leaving the row dirty on a server rejection is *correct* — the engine must not silently drop unsynced data — so this is not a sync-engine bug; the defect is purely the missing columns.)
- **Scope note (hypothesis refuted / refined).** Not an ADR-0009 ordering issue and not an ADR-0005 redaction edge (debts are non-redacted couple-shared data). The bug is **specific to the paid-for-partner path** because that's the only debt path that sends a non-null `source_transaction_id`; a **manually** entered debt sends no source txn, and a plain **settlement** payment leaves `is_netting`/`counter_debt_id` at their defaults — so whether those two paths also break depends solely on whether the supabase-kt Json encodes null/default fields (`encodeDefaults`). Probe #3 proved that even an explicit `source_transaction_id: null` still returns `PGRST204`, so if the SDK encodes nulls, manual debts break too; if it omits them, only paid-for-partner (and, on the payments table, netting) breaks — which lines up with the tester reporting *only* the paid-for-partner flow. Either way the fix below resolves all cases.

**Proposed fix:** Align staging (and, when it exists, prod) with `schema.sql` by adding the three missing columns — a **schema migration, no Kotlin change**. Add a new file `supabase/migrations/2026-07-06_partner_debt_missing_columns.sql` and apply it to staging:

```sql
alter table partner_debts
    add column if not exists source_transaction_id uuid;

alter table partner_debt_payments
    add column if not exists is_netting boolean not null default false,
    add column if not exists counter_debt_id uuid references partner_debts(id) on delete cascade;

-- PostgREST caches the schema; nudge a reload so the new columns are visible immediately.
notify pgrst, 'reload schema';
```

No data backfill and no client cleanup are needed: the stuck debt rows are still `pending_sync=1` locally, so once staging accepts the column the **very next sync pushes and clears them automatically** — the sign-out guard clears itself and no data was lost. Recommend also verifying the three columns via the same PostgREST `select=` probe after applying, and (belt-and-suspenders) confirming no *other* table in `schema.sql` has drifted off staging the same way, since the missing-migration pattern here suggests the migrations folder is not a complete record of what's live.

## Item 5 — State not saving when backgrounding app <30s

- **Status:** DONE `fea0cff` — `GoalEditorViewModel` mirrors its draft into `SavedStateHandle` per the plan below; JVM round-trip test added and passing (`GoalEditorViewModelTest`). Dialog-editor follow-up (Accounts/Categories/Budgets) left as a separate future slice.
- **Dev comment:** State not saving when backgrounding app even for less than 30s.

Not app-lock: the 30s grace (`AppLockManager`) is unrelated to in-progress screen state. **Top hypothesis:** either genuine **process death**, or a specific editor (NoteEditor / AddTransaction) holding in-progress input in **plain ViewModel state rather than `SavedStateHandle`**, lost on `onStop`/recreation.
**Repro:** enable **Developer Options → "Don't keep activities"** to force recreation deterministically; type into each editor, background, return; identify which screen drops input and whether it's process death vs. a specific screen's un-saved state.

**Findings (repro):**
It is **not** process death and **not** a global bug — it is specific screens whose draft lives in **plain ViewModel `MutableStateFlow` state that is never mirrored into `SavedStateHandle`** (and whose screen has no `rememberSaveable` fallback). With **Developer Options → "Don't keep activities"** the effect is identical to process death for these screens: `always_finish_activities` finishes the Activity on background *without* a config change, so the `ViewModelStore` is **cleared** (ViewModels are only retained across config changes, not across finish-and-recreate). On return, `SavedStateHandle`-backed drafts are restored from the saved-instance bundle while plain VM fields are re-initialized to blank.

Note: on-device confirmation with "Don't keep activities" enabled was attempted but blocked — the target is Alvin's personal handset, which was OS-locked/dozing, and the app-lock screen sets `FLAG_SECURE` (black `screencap`, no `uiautomator` tree). The mechanism below is established by code inspection and is directly corroborated by the differential hardening comments already in each ViewModel.

Per-screen result:
- **NoteEditor — survives.** Title + HTML live in the composable's `rememberSaveable` (`NoteEditorScreen.kt:76-77`); the un-saveable `RichTextState` is mirrored into `draftHtml` via `snapshotFlow` and re-seeded on recreation (`:89-97`). VM mirrors the stable note id + share intent into `SavedStateHandle` (`NoteEditorViewModel.kt:53,127`). Comment at `:73-75` documents this as intentional (Slice 1B).
- **AddTransaction — survives.** Every field mutation is written through `setEditor()` into `SavedStateHandle` and rehydrated by `hydrateFromSaved()` (`AddTransactionViewModel.kt:210-258`). Comment at `:34-38` documents this explicitly ("mirrored into `SavedStateHandle` … so it survives process death").
- **Savings Goal editor — LOSES INPUT (the bug).** `GoalEditorViewModel` keeps the entire editable draft — `name`, `targetText`, `targetDate`, `icon`, `color`, and the new-goal `isShared` intent — in a plain `MutableStateFlow<GoalEditorUiState>` with **no `SavedStateHandle` writes** (`GoalEditorViewModel.kt:37,74-96`), and `GoalEditorScreen` binds straight to `viewModel.uiState` with **no `rememberSaveable`** fallback (`GoalEditorScreen.kt:54,88-101`). On recreation `init` re-runs and, for a new goal, resets to a blank state with a freshly minted UUID (`:41-42`) — all typed input is gone. This is the clearest full-screen reproduction of the dev's report.
- **Dialog editors (Accounts / Categories / Budgets) — also lose input, lower severity.** Each holds its `*EditorState` in the list ViewModel's plain `MutableStateFlow` with no `SavedStateHandle` (e.g. `AccountsViewModel.kt:42`, `AccountEditorDialog` at `AccountsScreen.kt:181`). On recreation the VM clears, `editor` becomes `null`, and the dialog closes losing input. Severity is lower (a dismissed dialog on recreation is a more conventional loss than a full-screen editor blanking), but the same root cause applies.

**Proposed fix:**
Make `GoalEditorViewModel` mirror its draft into `SavedStateHandle`, following the **AddTransactionViewModel pattern** exactly (single `setState()` write-through + `hydrateFromSaved()` on init) rather than the NoteEditor `rememberSaveable` pattern (which suits a composable-owned `RichTextState` but not this VM-owned form):
- Inject/keep `savedStateHandle` (already injected) and add draft keys for `name`, `targetText`, `targetDate` (store as epoch-day `Long?`), `icon`, `color`, and `isShared` (new-goal intent), plus the stable `goalId` UUID so a resumed save doesn't orphan under a new id (same rationale as `NoteEditorViewModel.KEY_NOTE_ID`).
- Route every `onXChange`/`toggleShared` mutation through a private `setState { … }` helper that updates `_uiState` **and** writes the mirrored keys — mirroring `AddTransactionViewModel.setEditor()`.
- In `init`, prefer a `hydrateFromSaved()` result over both the blank-new-goal branch and the DB-loaded branch (so a restored draft wins over re-loading from Room), matching `AddTransactionViewModel.init`'s `restored != null` precedence.
- Clear the mirrored keys on successful `save()` (parallel to `clearDraft()`).
- Do **not** move fields into a composable `rememberSaveable`: the form is VM-owned and validated in the VM, so keeping the source of truth in the VM + `SavedStateHandle` is the consistent choice.
- Add a JVM unit test asserting round-trip through `SavedStateHandle` restores the draft (tier-1: this is state-restoration logic, cheap to test).
- **Follow-up (separate, lower priority):** apply the same `SavedStateHandle` mirroring to the Accounts/Categories/Budgets dialog `*EditorState` in their list ViewModels, or accept dialog dismissal as expected — decide per-screen. Track as its own slice; the Goal editor is the headline fix.

## Item 6 — Edit Navbar blocks changing modules

- **Status:** DONE `abf9ffd` — root-level route, on-device verified. Chose the root-route option over the broader switchTab-guard alternative per Alvin's confirmation. It's a **nav-graph placement bug** interacting with the `switchTab` save/restore machinery (ADR-0033/0039), not a disabled tab bar.
- **Dev comment:** while in Edit Navbar the changing of module is getting blocked, user would hae to click 'back' to go to other modules

**Top hypothesis:** interaction with the ADR-0039 `switchTab` guard (which pops a non-tab **root-level** route before navigating) while the navbar editor is open — or the tab bar is intentionally disabled/consumed while the editor is up. Needs repro against current `main` and a look at where the navbar editor sits in the nav graph (root route vs. in-graph).
**Repro:** open Edit Navbar → tap another module tab → confirm it's blocked until "back" is pressed → inspect the editor's nav placement and the `switchTab` path.

**Findings (repro):** Reproduced on an emulator (Medium_Phone, stagingDebug) driven via `uiautomator`. The tab bar is **not** disabled — taps reach `switchTab` — but for the common case the navigate is a **silent no-op**, leaving the editor on screen. Pressing Back pops the editor and normal tab switching resumes, exactly matching "have to click back."

- **Where the editor sits.** `NAV_EDITOR_ROUTE` is declared **inside the Settings nested graph** (`IponApp.kt:348`, within `navigation(route = SETTINGS.graphRoute())`), **not** as a root-level route like `ADD_TRANSACTION_ROUTE`. It is reached by a plain `navController.navigate(NAV_EDITOR_ROUTE)` from the More sheet (`:400`) and from Personalize (`:331`).
- **Why ADR-0039's guard doesn't catch it.** `switchTab` (`:434-452`) only pops the current top before navigating when it is **not** inside any module graph: `if (!inSomeModuleGraph) popBackStack()` (`:438-440`). Settings **is** a registered module (`NavRegistry.all`, `NavDestination.kt:67`), so sitting on the editor evaluates `inSomeModuleGraph == true` and the ADR-0039 pop is **skipped**. `switchTab` then runs the standard tab navigate — `navigate(dest.graphRoute()){ popUpTo(rootStart){ saveState = true }; launchSingleTop = true; restoreState = true }` (`:446-450`) — with the editor still on top.
- **The confirmed trigger — a doubled module-graph stack.** Opening the editor pushes the **Settings graph on top of the origin tab's graph** (plain `navigate`, no save/pop), so **two** module graphs are live at once (e.g. `records_graph` under `settings_graph/nav_editor`). At that point `switchTab`'s `popUpTo(rootStart){saveState}` + `restoreState=true` cannot resolve the target tab over the doubled stack, and the navigate **does nothing** whenever the target tab already has saved back-stack state.
  - **Directly observed, deterministic:** from the editor, tapping a tab that had been visited earlier (Analysis, Records — has saved state) is a **no-op**; tapping a **never-visited** tab (Manage, first use — no saved state) **navigates**. First-ever switch to a tab works; every subsequent one is blocked. (Also observed the ADR-0039 resurrection class here — the editor reappearing on top of a tab after a switch — the same save/restore machinery misbehaving.)
- **Differential that isolates the cause (rules out "any sub-screen").** A non-Settings sub-screen does **not** block: `Records → Recurring` (Recurring is `IponApp.kt:253`, in `records_graph`), then tapping the saved-state Analysis tab **navigates fine**. The difference is graph count: reaching Recurring stays **within the single** `records_graph` (the origin tab's own graph), so only one module graph is live; reaching the editor **stacks a second** graph (Settings) over the origin tab. So the defect is specific to destinations that are pushed as a *separate module graph over the current tab* — the editor today — not to sub-screens in general.

**Fix implemented:** promoted the navbar editor to a **root-level route**, a sibling of `ADD_TRANSACTION_ROUTE` outside every module graph (amends nothing in ADR-0033 dec. 2's spirit; it's the same "standalone screen reached from several places" shape as Add/Edit). `IponApp.kt`: moved the `composable(NAV_EDITOR_ROUTE) { NavbarEditorScreen(...) }` block out of the Settings nested graph and placed it alongside `ADD_TRANSACTION_ROUTE`. Both entry points (`navigate(NAV_EDITOR_ROUTE)` from More and from Personalize) needed no change. Chose this over the broader switchTab-guard alternative (which would've needed doubled-graph back-stack detection, more blast radius against ADR-0039's Add-over-Recurring case) per a quick confirmation with Alvin.

**Verified on-device** (emulator, `Medium_Phone`, stagingDebug, via `uiautomator`): from the editor, tapping a previously-visited tab (Records — has saved state, was the reproduced no-op) now navigates on the first tap; returning to another tab (Analysis) shows no editor resurrection. Add/Edit + deep sub-screen cases (Records → Recurring) untouched by this change (different route, same guard).

## Item 7 — Uncategorised debt transactions

- **Status:** DONE `ae64ceb`.
- **Dev comment:** User paying a debt, uncategorized. User adding to account a debt payment, uncategorized.

Not a data bug: settlement legs (`SettleDebtUseCase`, `AddSettlementIncomeUseCase`) are created with `categoryId = null` + `isSettlement = true` **by design** (count toward balance, excluded from Analysis — ADR-0019 #14). The issue is that Records labels them "Uncategorized." **Decision:** add a display-only branch in `TransactionsViewModel` rendering any `isSettlement` row as **"Debt settlement"** — a single label for both legs, keyed off the existing flag, mirroring the existing `TRANSFER → "Transfer"` branch. **No real category** (would pollute the picker/budgets and re-enter Analysis). The "paid for partner" *original* expense is a normally-categorized purchase and is out of scope. Full rationale in **ADR-0042**.

## Item 8 — Truncated "shared" tagging on Manage module

- **Status:** DONE 35c4e2b
- **Dev comment:** Truncated "shared" tagging on manage module.

**Cause:** in the Manage screens the entity-name `Text` is placed in a `Row` **before** `SharedBadge()` with no width constraint (e.g. `AccountsScreen` account-name row). A long account/category name eats the horizontal space and squeezes the badge against the edge, clipping its " Shared" text. **Decision:** the entity name gets `weight(1f, fill = false)` + `maxLines = 1` + ellipsis, and the `SharedBadge` is protected from shrinking so its label never truncates (a clipped *name* is normal; a clipped *status tag* is the bug). Apply the rule **uniformly at every `SharedBadge` call site** (accounts, categories, savings) so it can't regress in one screen. Pure UI — no ADR.

---

## Item 9 — Use "shared" tagging in Notes instead of heart icon

- **Status:** DONE `6c5ec4f`.
- **Dev comment:** Instead of heart tagging in Notes, use "shared" for consistency.

Notes marks my-shared notes (`isShared`) with a ❤️ (`NotesScreen` / `NoteEditorScreen`) and partner notes with a "From {Partner}" text label. **Decision:** replace the heart with the canonical **`core/ui/SharedBadge`** (People-icon + "Shared" pill, already used by accounts/categories/savings) for the `isShared` case; **leave "From {Partner}" untouched** for partner notes (it carries authorship/direction a generic "Shared" pill would lose). Reuses the existing component (Scalability Principle: sharing UI stays generic). Pairs naturally with Item 8's badge-layout rule. Pure UI — no ADR.
